## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Uppādavāra* ("Origination Section", Ya 2.2.1) forms the opening section of the *Pavattivāra* (process section) in the second chapter of the *Yamaka*, the sixth book of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral; Ronkin 2005]. Within the overarching framework of the *Yamaka*, doctrinal categories are methodically evaluated through a process division consisting of three successive cycles: origination (*uppādavāra*), cessation (*nirodhavāra*), and combined origination-cessation (*uppādanirodhavāra*) [Gal 2003; Ronkin 2005; Anderson 1999]. In this section, the analysis systematically examines the arising of phenomena across the three temporal periods (present, past, and future) according to analytical frames: with regard to person (*puggala*), realm or place (*okāsa*), and both person and place jointly (*puggalokāsa*), tested under both positive (*anuloma*) and negative (*paccanīka*) pairings [Nyanatiloka 2007].
Scholars note that the *Pavattivāra* analyses—beginning with the *Uppādavāra*—exemplify an early Buddhist process metaphysics, conceptualizing experience in terms of dynamic processes rather than enduring substances [Gal 2003; Ronkin 2005]. These sections are also doctrinally significant for documenting the early Abhidhamma development of momentary analysis (*khaṇa*), distinguishing specific sub-moments such as the origination-moment (*uppādakkhaṇa*) and dissolution-moment (*bhaṅgakkhaṇa*) [Gal 2003; Ronkin 2005].
According to DharmaNexus, the *Uppādavāra* exhibits immense internal text reuse across the Pali Abhidhamma (7,609 matches across 32 texts) [DharmaNexus]. Its highest levels of text sharing occur with its complementary counterpart sections in the same chapter—the *Nirodhavāra* (Ya 2.2.2; 1,292 matches) and the *Uppādanirodhavāra* (Ya 2.2.3; 1,242 matches)—as well as corresponding *Uppādavāra* sections in other *Yamaka* chapters, particularly those of the *Indriya-yamaka* (Ya 10.2.1) and *Āyatana-yamaka* (Ya 3.2.1), and the *Abhidhammamātikāpāḷi* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus identifies no cross-language matches meeting significance thresholds, and SuttaCentral registers one translation [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
